source.title: From Statistical Physics to Algorithms in Deep Neural Systems

record.file_problem: Full doctoral dissertation text is present. No apparent truncation or garbling affects the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The dissertation reports its own gradient-based training results on binary perceptron and stochastic neural network models, measuring training classification error. The deep-network results use MNIST and do not directly reproduce the CIFAR settings in V1.
record.gate_note: The dissertation discusses or cites material related to local minima, depth, initialization, learning rates, and batch normalization, but those discussions are not its own tests of V2–V6. The rows below cover the dissertation's own reported training-error results. Table 3.1 reports separate optimizer/dropout conditions; Table 3.2 reports separate methods. Figure 2.9 gives plotted error values without recoverable exact numbers.
record.test_reason: The dissertation reports optimization results, but none tests a listed version. Its perceptron and fully connected binary-network experiments differ from V1's convolutional CIFAR training setting; its LeNet-5 experiments investigate connectivity between selected MNIST solutions. It provides no controlled tests of V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is partly accurate, but it overstates the evidence for training-set error and attributes the explicit TCM zero-error statement to LeNet-5. The authors conclude that stochastic relaxation enables binary-perceptron optimization, accessible solution regions exhibit connectivity, the deep stochastic extension underperforms leading convolutional heuristics, and sensitivity-based regularization substantially reduces parameters while preserving or improving generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The dissertation studies stochastic binary synapses and version-space paths, rather than standard SGD/Adam training of large real-valued convolutional networks on CIFAR benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: For the fully-connected stochastic MNIST network, the reported binary error changes with optimizer and input/hidden dropout settings (Table 3.1).

fits_no_version.finding: The stochastic binary perceptron reaches an algorithmic storage capacity of approximately 0.63; slower thermalization brings its error curve closer to theoretical predictions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A continuous stochastic relaxation permits gradient-based learning of binary-perceptron solutions, with success depending on storage load and annealing.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 3.1 and 3.2 compare binary-network classification performance across optimizers, dropout choices and Monte Carlo sampling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stochastic binary fully connected networks achieve low MNIST classification error, with performance varying across training methods.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors find connecting paths between algorithmically obtained solutions in TCMs and LeNet-5 MNIST experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected gradient-trained solutions can belong to a connected region of the classification solution space.

fits_no_version.finding: The stochastic convolutional extension performs worse than the cited BinaryNet comparator, which the authors attribute to an inadequate Gaussian approximation for small filters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The stochastic binary-network approximation loses effectiveness when extended to convolutional architectures.

record.problems: The main deep-network results use MNIST rather than CIFAR; the architecture is fully connected rather than convolutional. Table 3.1 and Table 3.2 report results averaged over 10 seeds, but most sections do not state uncertainty. Fig. 2.9 and Fig. 3.10 provide plotted outcomes without exact values. The convolutional result's 'about 0.78% of accuracy' wording is ambiguous.
record.rows_left_out: No reported training-error results bearing on V1 were left out. The dissertation's cited prior-work results and its theoretical discussions were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Training fit of sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels, and the stated size, early-stopping and regularization qualifications.
Spurious-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction with one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, matched identity-shortcut comparisons, and the special-initialization exceptions.
Comparative effects of initialization on learning speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to the initial stability limit, including recovery, edge-of-stability behavior and divergence.
Matched normalization comparisons of training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free residual training.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both V1 verdicts. Above-zero classification errors with an unspecified evaluation split cannot establish incomplete training fit, and results outside the specified architectures and datasets do not qualify V1's scope. No missing result in the supplied text directly tests V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random-label or corrupted-label benchmarks, convolutional architecture training error, and comparisons involving model size or early stopping are not tested in the reported results.
